study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Wu and Baeken, Biological Psychiatry: Global Open Science, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Sex Determines Anterior Cingulate Cortex Cortical Thickness in the Course of Depression

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Assess whether sex differences influence anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) cortical thickness (CT) across the course of major depressive disorder (first-episode vs recurrent), leveraging linear mixed-effects models and normative modeling.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly states that structural brain imaging data were obtained from the REST-meta-MDD Consortium, which consists of 25 research groups in 17 hospitals in China. The final analysis used data from 9 study sites after applying quality and sample size exclusion criteria.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Structural brain imaging data were used from the REST-MetaMDD Consortium (35), which consists of 25 research groups in 17 hospitals in China... Consequently, 499 patients with MDD (381 first-episode MDD, 118 recurrent MDD) and 524 HCs with an age range of 12 to 77 years were selected from 9 study sites.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Females show thinner ACC CT than males; sex modulates ACC CT across depression course: FE females thinner than FE males; FE males thicker than recurrent males and than healthy males; effects localized to emotional ACC (pgACC/sgACC); no lateralization differences.
